# Evaluation Engineering

> A working wiki on evaluation engineering: the discipline of designing, building, and operating systems that produce large numbers of estimates and evaluations at known cost. Maintained by QURI as part of the CAIRN project.

Sibling wiki: Robust Reasoning Processes (https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org), on reasoning processes that resist corruption.


## Start Here

- [1. Evaluation Engineering](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/start-here/introduction/): What evaluation engineering is, why treat evaluation as a systems problem, and what the field is trying to build.
- [2. Estimation vs. Evaluation](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/start-here/estimation-vs-evaluation/): The field's foundational distinction — clean quantitative estimation vs. messy judgment-bound evaluation — and the divide-and-conquer design strategy it implies.
- [3. Why It Matters — Use Cases](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/start-here/use-cases/): Concrete things highly optimized evaluation systems would unlock — futarchy, certificates of impact, felicific calculators, Guesstimate-scale tooling, and charity prioritization.
- [4. Cruxes](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/start-here/key-questions/): The open questions evaluation engineering turns on — the things that, if resolved, would most change the shape of the field.

## Part I — The Systems View

- [5. Evaluation as a System](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/the-systems-view/): Why an evaluation system is a different object from an evaluation, and the accuracy × quantity × cost trade-offs that define its design space.
- [6. The Four Components](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/components/): Prediction, calculation, ontology, and evaluation — the reusable parts that show up in every serious evaluation system, plus the background they sit on.

## Part II — Methods & Techniques

- [7. Evaluation Methods](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/evaluation-methods/): The catalogue of concrete ways to produce evaluations — expert panels, surveys, review systems, statistical measures, and composite indices — with their cost and trust profiles.
- [8. Techniques](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/techniques/): The system-level patterns that tie the components together — prediction–evaluation systems, scalable structured forecasting, estimation functions, and automated trust networks.
- [9. LLMs as Evaluators](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/llm-evaluators/): What language models change in an evaluation system — which components they cheapen, what the LLM-as-judge literature measures about their reliability, the two system-level failures (correlated error and Goodhart), and how to use them as the cheap layer of a prediction–evaluation system.
- [Interlude: A Worked Example](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/worked-example/): One evaluation problem — a funder reviewing 1,000 grants a year — carried through four system designs with explicit costs, what each design can and cannot learn, and the arithmetic behind a 50-item audit.

## Part III — Evidence from the Wild

- [10. Evaluation Systems in the Wild](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/evaluation-systems-in-the-wild/): A catalogue of ~100 real-world evaluation systems — from RTINGS and IMDb to credit ratings, Michelin, and the Corruption Perceptions Index — and what they teach about building evaluation systems.
- [11. Patterns & Failure Modes](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/patterns-and-failure-modes/): What the academic literature establishes across real-world evaluation systems — reactivity, Goodhart's law, selection bias, certification economics, reputation inflation, and aggregation theory — and what it implies for evaluation engineering.

## Part IV — The Environment

- [12. Epistemic Culture](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/concepts/epistemic-culture/): Why culture, not technology, is plausibly the binding constraint on evaluation systems — and what cultural engineering for candidness might look like.

## Reference

- [Glossary](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/reference/glossary/): Key terms used across the evaluation-engineering wiki.
- [Objections & FAQ](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/reference/objections/): The strongest objections to evaluation engineering, the responses on offer, the cost/scale picture, and external commentary.
- [Lineage](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/start-here/lineage/): Where evaluation engineering comes from — the 2021–22 "advanced / symbolic evaluation systems" program and what changed with LLMs.
- [Related Work (QURI)](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/reference/related-work/): QURI's published work that this wiki draws on — the framing, the deployed tools, and the scarce empirical results behind evaluation engineering.
- [Adjacent Fields & Literature](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/reference/adjacent-fields/): The mature literatures evaluation engineering draws on — forecasting, decision analysis, program evaluation, LLM evals, scalable oversight, and estimation/ontology tooling — with entry-point citations.
- [Open Problems](https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org/open-questions/): A running, aggregated list of the unresolved problems in evaluation engineering.
